model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the evolution of trade balances, exports, and imports over time, with values measured in billions of US dollars. The x-axis represents years, ranging from 2020 to 2023, with tick marks indicating annual intervals. The y-axis is dual-scaled: the left side ranges from 0 to 400 billion US dollars and corresponds to exports and imports, while the right side ranges from -200 to 400 billion US dollars and corresponds to the trade balance (Saldo). The blue line, representing imports (left scale), starts at approximately 200 billion US dollars in 2020, dips to around 150 billion US dollars in early 2021, and then rises steadily to over 300 billion US dollars by late 2023. The purple line, representing exports (left scale), begins at about 130 billion US dollars in 2020, declines to roughly 90 billion US dollars in early 2021, and then gradually increases to approximately 170 billion US dollars by late 2023. The blue bars, representing the trade balance (right scale), are consistently negative from 2020 to 2023, starting at around -100 billion US dollars in 2020, dipping to approximately -200 billion US dollars in early 2021, and then recovering to about -100 billion US dollars by late 2023.
